note.text: 4.c3 prepares d4. Against ...Nf6 White plays a quiet d3 first; against the passive ...d6, d4 straight away.
3...Be7 is passive, so White strikes in the centre with d4. After ...exd4, take back and enjoy the better centre.

nodes.name: Italian Game: Two Knights Defense, Modern Bishop's Opening

note.text: 4.d3 protects e4, so the knight on f6 has nothing to take. This is the quiet way: castle, play c3, and push d4 only when you are ready.
3...d6 is solid but shuts in Black's bishop on f8. White develops calmly with c3 and castling. If Black plays ...Nf6, Ng5 hits the weak f7 square.
3...h6 stops Ng5 but brings out no piece. White hits the centre at once while Black is a move behind.
Take the knight. Most players grab the e5 pawn instead with Nxe5, and lose a piece after ...Qg5, which attacks the knight and g2 at once.
3...f5 is a gamble. Taking with exf5 lets ...e4 hit the knight; d3 keeps e4 covered. Black's king is now weak on the diagonal from c4 to g8.

nodes.name: Italian Game: Classical Variation, Giuoco Pianissimo

note.text: 5.d3 guards e4, so the knight cannot take it. Castle next, then think about a4, b4 or a slow d4.
Castle first: the king is safe and the rook can come to e1 later. Next is c3, which prepares d4.
Against the modest ...Be7, castle and play c3 or Re1. The centre stays closed and both sides manoeuvre.
Take the pawn: 4...d5 opens the centre while White is ready for it. After ...Nxd5, castle and then aim at the knight in the middle.
4...d6 shuts in the bishop on f8, and f7 has only the king to guard it. Ng5 attacks f7 with the knight and the bishop at once.
4...h6 is slow, so White brings out another piece. Castling comes next; there is no hurry.
Take back with the knight, which sits well in the centre. If Black trades knights, the queen recaptures and rules the board.
White is a clean pawn up. Develop simply with castling and c3 to open lines against the pawn on d4.

note.text: 6.c3 prepares d4 and takes the d4 square away from Black's knight. White keeps the centre closed for now and improves with h3, Re1 and Nbd2.
Two pawns in the centre, and the bishop on c5 must move. ...Bb4+ looks active, but Nc3 blocks it and White keeps the big centre.

nodes.name: Italian Game: Classical Variation, Giuoco Pianissimo

note.text: Castle, then h3, Re1 and Nbd2. White's pieces gather on the kingside while the centre stays closed.
6.h3 takes g4 away from Black's bishop before it can pin the knight. Then c3, Re1 and Nbd2, the same plan as before.

nodes.name: Italian Game: Classical Variation, Giuoco Pianissimo

note.text: The same plan as against castling: c3 first, ready for d4 or b4. ...h6 only stopped Bg5 and Ng5.
The king is safe, and Re1 puts pressure on e5. The knight on d5 can be chased with c3 and d4, or with Nc3.
The queen on d4 is strong and hard to chase away. White is ahead in development and stands clearly better.

note.text: 7.h3 stops ...Bg4, which would pin the knight on f3. Now Re1 and Nbd2 can follow without the pin.
7.b4 gains space and chases the bishop. After ...Bb6, a4 threatens to push on and trap it.
Castle and keep the big centre. Then h3 and Nc3, and d5 at the right moment pushes Black's pieces back.
Block with the knight: it develops and guards e4 and d5. White castles next and can push d5 to gain more space.

note.text: The rook backs up e4 and gets ready for d4 one day. The knight on b1 usually travels to d2, f1 and g3.
8.a4 threatens a5, and the bishop on b6 would have no good square. Black usually makes room with ...a6 or ...a5.
